answer: Reputation-gated task admission. Each identity's score is the running product of signed peer ratings, logged per task in a shared orchard of records. New clones start at zero and can only enter cheap tasks, whose ratings carry a fixed audit sample; a clone farm must complete and audit k tasks per identity before reaching paid work. Since audit cost per rating exceeds clone-task revenue (a gale of low-value work nets nothing), and any single flagged rating collapses the chain down a canyon, marginal cloning is negative-EV. Attackers pay audit plus forgone revenue per identity.
